scope: Ablation of all work that was uncommitted before this task: project loading, four IDE items and P1 semantics. The initial checkpoint was committed before experiments.

source.result: Uncommitted simplifications on the checkpoint; historical baselines preserved.
source.hash_method: SHA256 of sorted rg --files paths (*.rs, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, rust-toolchain.toml), each path + NUL + contents + NUL.

method.negative_trials: Six independent mutations of the checkpoint. Each compiled, reached a named failing test, and was restored before the next trial. Patches are embedded for reproduction against the checkpoint.
method.positive_trials: Five cumulative simplifications, one at a time, each with focused checks, followed by combined full-workspace, corpus, model and incremental verification. This is not a factorial experiment or proof of equivalence for all inputs.
method.compile_retry: The first S3 attempt missed a removed public re-export. It was restored and retried with that export adjusted. The compile failure is not counted as semantic ablation evidence; local log: target/ablation/2026-10-24/S3-export-adjustment.log
method.reproduction: Use an isolated checkout at checkpoint_commit for each negative patch and run its recorded command. Positive patches are local artifacts; the retained source diff is the reviewable combined implementation.

restored_experiments.reason_to_retain: Lexical annotation constraints must resolve inside the active shadowing scope; signature expectations have different binding semantics.
Strict bitvector mode must prove nonnegative widths recursively, including list elements and generic declarations.
Undefined generation must be valid for the generic declaration; a concrete register argument cannot rescue an invalid generic generator.
The extraction workspace edit must carry the open source document version. This experiment isolates the version field, not every stale-edit guard.
Typed missing-field metadata enables appropriate defaults and generic field instantiation in fixes.
A missing manifest source must not prevent loading existing project files; recovery must observe the missing source when it appears.

strict.exit_explanation: The command also checks extended corpora; seven preexisting false-positive files keep its exit code at 1. The requested strict typecheck suite has zero acceptance/rejection disagreements.

default.note: The directory expectations are strict-mode expectations. The live default-mode compiler also accepts negative_bits_list; all other six targeted cases are rejected in both modes.

extended.note: Unchanged from the preceding baseline. The full conformance command exits 1 for these existing extended-corpus errors; the requested typecheck suite has no acceptance/rejection disagreement.

riscv.note: Expression, diagnostic and deferred-constraint totals match the checkpoint baseline. Wall times were collected concurrently with corpus validation and do not isolate performance changes.

incremental.method: Four serialized probes after corpus validation, one run per size/mode, 32 edits each.
incremental.finding: Reinference scope unchanged: body edits 1 at 160 files and 1-2 at 1600 files; signature edits 3. Large-case edit p95 was 14.991 ms body and 15.080 ms signature. No large regression observed; single-run noise does not establish a speedup or rust-analyzer performance parity.

remaining_limitations: Seven false positives in the separate extended upstream corpora.
Diagnostic location/wording parity is tracked separately from acceptance/rejection.
576 unknown deferred constraints remain on the pinned RISC-V manifest; they are not unknown expression types.
